Phenytoin is considered unsafe in porphyric pa- tients; it would be prudent to assume that this consideration also applied to its prodrug, fosphenytoin. Interactions As for Phenytoin, p.497. Pharmacokinetics Plasma concentrations of fosphenytoin are maximal at the end of intravenous infusion and about 30 minutes after intramuscular injection. Protein binding of fosphenytoin is high (95 to 99%), mainly to albumin, and is saturable. Fosphenytoin displaces phenytoin from protein binding sites which increases the fraction of unbound phenytoin to up to 30% for about half to one hour post-infusion. Fosphenytoin is rapidly and completely hydrolysed to phenytoin with a conversion half-life of about 15 minutes; one mmol of fospheny- toin yields one mmol of phenytoin, and the same of phosphate and formate. Metabolites of phenytoin are excreted in the urine. For the pharmacokinetics of phenytoin, see p.500. ◊ References. 1. Fischer JH, et al.
